Let me analyze these teaching examples carefully to identify systematic forecast errors and derive correction rules.

Looking at the examples, they all appear to be dated around August 2024 and involve EU ETS (carbon) price forecasting with 30-day horizons.

Let me examine the patterns:

**Example 1 (2024-11-28)** - This is actually after the August examples, but let me look at it:
- History prices: starting around 65.22, trending up to 68.47
- Sentiment: mixed, many 0.00 values
- Model forecasts: starting around 68.18, gradually increasing
- True outcomes: starting around 67.63, but importantly the last 10-15 points are significantly LOWER than model forecasts (66.x range vs 68-70 in forecasts)

Wait, let me re-examine. Looking at Example 1's true outcomes vs forecasts:
- First 15 days out: Forecasts and outcomes are quite close (within 1-2 EUR)
- Days 16-20: Forecasts around 69.x, outcomes around 67.69 to 69.40 (minor differences)
- Days 21-25: Forecasts 70.64-70.08, outcomes 71.56-69.47 (under-predicted by ~1-2)
- Days 26-30: Forecasts 66.36-66.55, outcomes 74.85-66.14 (MAJOR divergence - under-predicted by 8-10 EUR!)

This looks like a lag or delayed reaction to a price spike around day 26-30.

**Example 2 (2024-08-05)**:
- History: prices around 64-71 EUR, some volatility
- Sentiment: ranging from -1.00 to 1.00
- Model forecasts: starting around 68.50, gradually increasing
- True outcomes: first 15 days match well, but then...


- Days 16-20: Forecasts 69.45-70.65, outcomes 70.49-71.49 (under by ~1)
- Days 21-25: Forecasts 69.28-70.39, outcomes 68.16-70.77 (under by ~1-2)
- Days 26-30: Forecasts 69.20-70.70, outcomes 66.50-64.92 (under by 3-6!)
